topics.topic: Scope of A08 rule 5 validation during installed-instance startup checks
questions: Which exact subset of A08 rule 5 is applied to a service record during start-up, and is it applied to every capability or only to service- and instance-level structure?
Which A08 rule 5 checks apply in `bindings.check_installed_instances` when that operation has no operation name or proposed ports with which to perform the operation-specific checks?
Which exact A08 checks are performed at startup, and are all capability entries validated or only the service and selected-instance structure needed for the credential-header collision check?

judgement.why: This asks the same startup manifest-validation scope and ordering question already decided by P5, and neither its deciding later-state passages nor the relevant change altered it.

precedent.topic: Scope and failure ordering of manifest validation during startup or installed-instance checks
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: Accepted API base URL forms, path joining, and resulting HTTP authority
questions: Which exact `api_base_url` forms are accepted, how are they joined to the declared path, and what exact authority becomes the default `Host` header?
May `api_base_url` contain user information, a query, a fragment, an existing path, or multiple trailing slashes, and exactly how are those cases joined with the declared path?

judgement.why: This asks the same API base-URL grammar, joining, authority and Host-header question already decided by P1, and neither its quoted passages nor the change altered it.

precedent.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and exact URL path, authority, slash, and Host handling
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

topics.topic: Checks required when submitting an existing equal contract version
questions: Does an equal existing contract version bypass the A02 validity and current-release ceiling checks?

topics.topic: Definition and handling of removable credential trailing newlines
questions: What counts as the one removable trailing newline: only LF, either LF or CRLF, or any final Unicode line break; and are additional trailing newlines rejected or retained?

topics.topic: Encoding or rejection of multipart parameter names and filenames

topics.topic: Error returned for missing records during captured trial-case creation
questions: Which error is returned when one of the records named by this operation does not exist?

topics.topic: Exact equality relation for JSON guard values

topics.topic: Handling of duplicate member names in installation JSON
questions: What does `installation.load_installation` do with duplicate JSON member names at the top level or inside its objects?

topics.topic: How manifest files are resolved at a revision and kept immutable during execution
questions: How does `bindings` resolve and read a file at `manifest_revision`, and what prevents files at the same configured revision from changing while the kernel is running?

topics.topic: How put_value_bytes reports digest or size mismatches and preserves request atomicity
questions: How must callers expose a digest or size mismatch from `put_value_bytes`, especially after earlier changes in the same surface request?

topics.topic: Outcome and storage behavior when an execution output exceeds the size limit
questions: How is an otherwise successful trial or admission execution classified when one value output exceeds stored_value_bytes_max, and is any output stored?

topics.topic: Permitted guard-port carriage and comparison semantics for file outputs
questions: Must a guard port have `value` carriage, or may a `file` output be used as a guard, and if so what file fact is compared with the guard value?

topics.topic: Public operation for validating a schema declaration without a candidate value
questions: Through which public operation does `functions` validate a schema declaration independently of any candidate value?

topics.topic: Representation accepted for authored file inputs and expected file outputs
questions: For authored file inputs and expected file outputs, does the operation receive file bytes, file facts, a transport attachment, or an existing value reference?

topics.topic: Representation of outputs in a direct try_implementation response
questions: Does a direct try_implementation response include resolved value outputs, StoredValue references, or only output digests?

topics.topic: Retry behavior for unchanged token-list configuration after a failed read
questions: While there is no valid token list, is the configuration retried on every request even when its bytes have the same digest as the last failed read, such as after a transient read or permission failure?

topics.topic: Store-position ordering for multiple records created by one change
questions: When one `record_change` creates several records, in what exact order are their distinct store positions assigned, including subordinate StoredValues or SpooledFiles and an AdmissionVerdict with its Activation?

topics.topic: Whether Run progress fields are mutable or derived from separate records
questions: Are Run.outputs, Run.waiting and Run.resumptions mutable fields of the Run row, or must progress be represented in separate records and derived without changing them?

topics.topic: Whether capture reuses or recreates a StoredValue when metadata differs
questions: When an existing StoredValue has a different disclosure class or stored schema from the contract input port, must capture create a new StoredValue over the same bytes, or reuse the existing reference?

topics.topic: Whether explicit try executions are durable and inspectable
questions: Are explicit try executions durably recorded and observable through inspection, or are they ephemeral results?

topics.topic: Whether file-carriage inputs can bind path placeholders
questions: May a `file` input port whose schema says string or integer satisfy a path placeholder at binding time?

topics.topic: Whether read_value_bytes enforces the run-spool lifecycle
questions: Does store.read_value_bytes itself enforce the run-spool lifecycle, or must it return lingering bytes whenever the caller supplies an existing SpooledFile identity?

topics.topic: Whether removing an unknown run spool is idempotent or an error
questions: Is an unknown run identity a successful idempotent removal or an `unknown_reference` error?

topics.topic: Which hosts qualify for the plain-HTTP loopback exception

topics.topic: Wire encoding and character restrictions for HTTP header values
